cases.input:
These are synthetic notes from a review of a desktop dictation application's settings synchronization. The discussion covered the custom vocabulary file, the settings store, and the file watcher. The team agreed to keep the investigation narrow. There is a report that a newly added word sometimes disappears from the visible list after a save, but nobody has reproduced that exact report yet. The report does not establish whether the file on disk loses the word or whether only the displayed state becomes stale. Both possibilities remain open, and the next investigation must distinguish them.

The current implementation writes a temporary file and then replaces custom_words.txt. The reviewer accepted that this can prevent readers from seeing a partially written file when replacement succeeds. It does not establish that all state changes occur in the right order. A watcher may have read the old file before the replacement and may publish that old snapshot after save_custom_words returns. That sequence is a hypothesis based on the code path, not an observed execution trace. No one should describe it as the confirmed root cause in the release notes.

A local experiment used version 0.6.2 and Rust 1.82.0. The file contained 240 entries before the edit and 241 entries after the successful save. In that experiment, the disk file still contained the new entry when inspected later. The interface briefly displayed 240 entries, but the observer did not capture enough timestamps to establish which callback supplied that state. This is evidence of a visible inconsistency in one local run. It is not evidence that every save loses data, and it is not sufficient to claim that the watcher hypothesis has been proven.

One proposed change was to add a second retry after publishing settings. Another was to attach a monotonically increasing revision to each snapshot. Neither proposal has been implemented or accepted. The reviewer asked the team to first capture the actual publication order using a small deterministic test or a bounded trace. The desired evidence should identify the revision read by the watcher, the revision written by the save, and the state eventually delivered to the frontend. The test should deliberately allow an older read to finish after a newer save, rather than relying on sleeps that may happen to trigger the sequence.

The team discussed filesystem events separately from application state. A successful replacement can generate multiple notifications, and those notifications do not necessarily correspond one to one with user edits. Deduplicating identical notifications might reduce unnecessary work, but it does not automatically solve stale publication. Similarly, serializing writes may protect two simultaneous saves while leaving a save-versus-watcher race untouched. The reviewer wants these claims kept separate so that a passing test for one boundary is not cited as proof of a different property.

There was also a small timing observation. A warm save of the sample list took 1.25 seconds on the developer's machine. Cold startup was not measured, the run was not repeated, and logging was enabled. No performance improvement or regression can be calculated from that observation. The team should not turn the number into a service target or use it to justify a cache. Performance work is outside this investigation unless the correctness fix introduces a measured problem that requires a separate decision.

For verification, the agreed immediate scope is the custom vocabulary path only. Do not reset all settings, reinstall the application, or change the model download code to make the symptom disappear. Preserve the user's existing vocabulary during any reproduction. All sample words used in the test will be invented and will contain no personal names or private identifiers. The frontend should still receive the same public event shape; any proposed contract change needs its own review. No decision was made about changing the storage format.

Finally, scheduling was discussed without making a release promise. Monday was suggested as a review opportunity if the ordering evidence is ready. It is not a committed fix date or a promised shipping date. Shipment remains on hold for this issue until the publication behavior has been checked and the reviewer can assess the evidence. The next update should report what was actually observed, which hypothesis remains uncertain, and whether a focused regression case can reproduce the inconsistency. It should not say that atomic replacement alone made the entire workflow safe.
cases.instruction: Summarize these notes in English in at most 150 words for an engineering reviewer. State observed evidence, the unconfirmed hypothesis, the next verification step, and the release/scheduling decision. Preserve key identifiers and numeric literals when included. Do not invent owners, deadlines, decisions, or completed work. Return only the summary.
rubric: Separate the observed stale interface and retained disk entry from the unconfirmed watcher-ordering explanation.
Explain that atomic replacement alone does not prove safe state publication.
Identify deterministic ordering evidence as the next step; neither retry nor revision proposal is accepted.
Preserve shipment hold and Monday's conditional review status without inventing a release date.
Prioritize correctness findings over incidental timing details within the word limit.
cases.reference: A local run on 0.6.2 showed 241 entries on disk after a save while the interface briefly showed 240; the callback responsible was not established. Atomic replacement of custom_words.txt does not prove publication ordering. A watcher publishing an old snapshot after save_custom_words returns is an unconfirmed hypothesis. Capture deterministic read, save, and publication ordering before selecting a fix; retries and revisions remain unaccepted proposals. Keep the investigation confined to vocabulary synchronization and preserve existing vocabulary and the frontend event contract. Shipment remains on hold pending review of that evidence. Monday is only a possible review opportunity, not a fix or release commitment. The single 1.25-second warm-save observation supports no performance conclusion.

cases.input:
This is a synthetic handover for a small reporting application used by a fictional workshop. The current change affects the preview window, not invoice calculation or payment collection. A tester reported a crash when closing a preview immediately after switching customers. The report mentions TFrmPreview and QueryCustomer, but it contains no stack trace that proves either object caused the crash. The developer could not reproduce it in three ordinary attempts. That result limits the evidence; it does not mean the report is invalid.

The main question is the lifetime relationship between the preview form, its visual controls, and the shared data module. Owner and Parent are different relationships in this application. A control can have a component owner that differs from its visual parent. The team must inspect both before deciding where to release anything. Someone suggested replacing several calls with FreeAndNil, but the reviewer did not approve that change. It could hide the symptom or introduce another lifetime error without explaining the original sequence.

The database query is SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions. In the provided synthetic database it returns 240 rows. With archived = 0 applied, it returns 180 rows. Those counts describe records, not unique active users, and they do not measure query speed. The team agreed to retain both values in the handover because the support question had confused session counts with people. No migration, deletion, or index change is authorized by these notes.

A proposed diagnostic run would open the preview, switch to a different customer, close the preview, and then inspect whether an asynchronous callback still tries to access it. This is a proposed investigation, not a confirmed reproduction recipe. The person doing it should capture the relevant callback order and identify which object is valid at each point. They should avoid resetting the test database between steps unless that reset is part of an explicitly recorded scenario. Otherwise, a supposedly successful retry could be testing a different state.

Separately, the workshop asked to move a training appointment from Tuesday to Thursday at 10:30. Thursday is only a proposed replacement, and the room is not confirmed. The existing Tuesday appointment must stay active until the new arrangement is confirmed. There was no promise to finish the software change before either appointment. The review request and the training booking are independent, even though they appeared in the same email thread.

The next engineering update should state whether the lifecycle trace was captured, what it shows, and which causes remain unverified. The next administrative update should confirm room availability or explicitly say it is still pending. There is no agreed release deadline. Keep the production database untouched, preserve the current booking, and avoid presenting a suggested diagnostic step as a completed fix.
cases.instruction: Summarize in English in at most 130 words for a handover. Separate the software investigation from the appointment request. Include the central lifetime uncertainty, SQL count distinction, proposed next diagnostic step, and booking constraint. Do not invent root causes, authorized changes, owners, or deadlines. Return only the summary.
rubric: Keep the crash report unconfirmed despite three unsuccessful reproduction attempts.
Distinguish Owner from Parent and avoid endorsing broad FreeAndNil replacement.
Keep 240 and 180 as session record counts, not users or performance measurements.
Describe callback-lifecycle tracing as proposed, not completed.
Keep Tuesday booked until the proposed Thursday 10:30 appointment is confirmed; invent no release deadline.
cases.reference: A reported preview-close crash remains unconfirmed. Inspect TFrmPreview's ownership, visual parenting, and callback lifetime: Owner and Parent differ, and broad FreeAndNil changes are unapproved. A proposed trace should check callbacks after customer switching and preview closure. The SQL results are 240 session records, or 180 with archived = 0, not active-user counts or performance evidence. Database changes are unauthorized. Separately, Thursday at 10:30 is a proposed training appointment with an unconfirmed room; retain Tuesday until confirmation. No software completion date or release deadline was agreed.

Drugi proces zakończył się poprawnie. Nie sprawdzono jednak zachowania z --no-tray, więc nie należy pisać, że wszystkie warianty CLI działają.

Na wersji 0.6.2 okno ustawień czasem pozostaje ukryte po użyciu --start-hidden. Problem wystąpił raz w czterech próbach. Nie wiadomo, czy przyczyną jest obsługa drugiej instancji, czy kolejność zdarzeń okna. Nie zatwierdzono zmian w send_transcription_input() ani w zapisie ustawień.

Zaproponowano zebranie krótkiego śladu zdarzeń i osobne sprawdzenie wariantu bez ikony w zasobniku. To następne kroki, nie wykonane testy. Nie ustalono osoby odpowiedzialnej ani daty zakończenia. Środa była jedynie propozycją dnia przeglądu, a nie terminem wydania.

W osobnym wątku poproszono o przyjazną odpowiedź klientowi w sprawie spotkania. Klient zaproponował piątek o 14:30, ale nie potwierdził sali. Obecne spotkanie w czwartek ma pozostać aktywne. Nie wolno powiązać terminu spotkania z obietnicą poprawki aplikacji.
cases.instruction: Podsumuj po polsku w maksymalnie 110 słowach. Oddziel potwierdzone obserwacje od hipotez i proponowanych testów. Uwzględnij ograniczenia dowodów, brak terminu wydania oraz niezależny wątek spotkania. Zachowaj identyfikatory flag. Nie dopisuj odpowiedzialnych osób ani zobowiązań. Zwróć tylko podsumowanie.
rubric: Zachowaj poprawne zachowanie drugiego procesu tylko w sprawdzonym wariancie.
Uwzględnij sporadycznie ukryte okno i nieznaną przyczynę.
Nie przedstawiaj śladu zdarzeń ani testu --no-tray jako wykonanych.
Zachowaj brak terminu wydania oraz propozycję środy jako przeglądu.
Oddziel niepotwierdzoną propozycję piątkowego spotkania od aktywnego czwartku i prac nad poprawką.
cases.reference: Sprawdzono poprawne przełączenie nagrywania przez --toggle-transcription i zakończenie drugiego procesu. Wariant --no-tray pozostaje niesprawdzony. Na 0.6.2 okno czasem pozostaje ukryte po --start-hidden; przyczyna jest nieznana. Zebranie śladu zdarzeń i test bez zasobnika to propozycje, bez przypisanego właściciela ani daty. Środa oznacza tylko proponowany przegląd, nie wydanie. Osobno: piątek o 14:30 i sala są niepotwierdzone, więc czwartkowe spotkanie pozostaje aktywne. Nie obiecano poprawki przed spotkaniem.
